title: The Plum Stands In for the Peach
era: Warring States · King Wei of Qi

source.book: Records of the Grand Historian, Biographies of Sun Tzu and Wu Qi
source.quote: Now match your lowest team against his highest, your highest against his middle, and your middle against his lowest.

moral: Give away one round to win the whole match — a small loss can buy the bigger win.

story.title: A Little Weaker Every Time
story.text: Three races, and every one of Tian Ji's horses was a little weaker.
story.narration: Tian Ji was going to race horses against King Wei of Qi — three races in all. He split his horses into top, middle and low, but each team was a little weaker than the king's matching team. Race them as they were, and he would lose all three.

story.title: Sun Bin's Idea
story.text: Sun Bin said: send our weakest against his strongest.
story.narration: Sun Bin watched for a while and said: send your lowest team against his highest and give that race away. Then send your highest against his middle, and your middle against his lowest — you win the last two. Two out of three, and the whole match is ours.

keyMoment.question: Every horse is a little weaker. How should they be matched up?

options.text: Our lowest against his highest, then win the other two
Our highest against his highest, to win the first race
options.hint: Six against seven cannot win — and our best horse is used up.

options.text: If our horses are weaker, don't race at all
options.hint: It is best of three: losing one race is not losing the match.

keyMoment.reveal: Give away the race you cannot win, and save your strength for the two you can — lose one, win the match.

misconceptions: If you are a little weaker at everything, you cannot win
You must fight hardest in every single round
Losing one round means losing the whole thing

quiz.question: Which of Tian Ji's horses did Sun Bin send against the king's highest?
quiz.explanation: The race against the highest team was given away on purpose, so the other two could be won.

quiz.question: In a best-of-three game you know you will lose the first round. What is the smarter plan?
options: Give away the weakest round and save your strength for the two you can win
Fight at full strength in every round
quiz.explanation: Let the round you cannot win go, and put your care into the two you can — the match is what counts.
